instruction.name: vld
instruction.description: Read whole vector from memory address `addr + offset`, save the data into `dst`. Address misalignment does not raise an exception. Note that you can use this intrinsic to load floating point vectors, even though the return type represents integer vectors.

experiments.name: pick-based address chase
experiments.init: addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r21, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r21; st.d $r0, $r20, 0; vreplgr2vr.d $vr0, $r0; xvreplgr2vr.d $xr0, $r0
experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 20000 --unroll2 40000 --iters 100 --warmup 10 --reps 10 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r21, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r21; st.d $r0, $r20, 0; vreplgr2vr.d $vr0, $r0; xvreplgr2vr.d $xr0, $r0' --asm 'vld $vr0, $r20, 0; vpickve2gr.d $r4, $vr0, 0; add.d $r20, $r20, $r4'

latencies.notes: L1D hit. The chain loads, moves the value to a GPR (3 cycles) and adds it to the base (1 cycle), so the load itself is 5 cycles. A vector load cannot bypass, so it is one cycle slower than an integer load, like a floating-point load.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r4, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r4' --asm 'vld $vr0, $r20, 0; vld $vr1, $r20, 16; vld $vr2, $r20, 32; vld $vr3, $r20, 48; vld $vr4, $r20, 64; vld $vr5, $r20, 80; vld $vr6, $r20, 96; vld $vr7, $r20, 112'
throughput.notes: 8 independent memory operations take 4.00 cycles. Buffer is 64-byte aligned; unaligned LASX loads/stores are substantially slower.

notes: L1D-hit vector load latency is 4 cycles, the same as the scalar floating-point loads.
